claims.text: An ab initio SQS–CPA framework will predict electrical conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr, including material with approximately 1 wt.% oxygen, within ±5% across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
Explicitly accounting for defects and oxygen-induced changes in electronic states and scattering will improve accuracy relative to defect-free analytical models.
As-synthesized bulk HfNbTaTiZr has inherent chemical disorder and point defects.
The modeled HfNbTaTiZr specimen has a controlled oxygen content of approximately 1 wt.%.
SQS representations can capture or approximate local atomic disorder in a chemically disordered alloy.
CPA efficiently averages configurational disorder in electronic-structure calculations and can treat arbitrary alloy concentrations.
The combined SQS–CPA implementation will include the influence of oxygen impurities in HfNbTaTiZr.
Quantum effects and defect-induced localized electronic states are significant for HfNbTaTiZr in the 0–200 K regime.
Phonon scattering and thermal excitations dominate conductivity in HfNbTaTiZr from 300 to 1200 K.
The framework is calibrated and verified against conductivity measurements from specimens containing approximately 1 wt.% oxygen.
Localized defect states and oxygen interstitials modify the ideal lattice potential and introduce additional carrier-scattering centers.
SQS defect configurations capture local atomic relaxations.
CPA can model disorder-averaged electronic density of states, but the cited evidence does not establish that it captures carrier scattering from the proposed defects and oxygen interstitials.
The modeled defect-induced electronic changes alter carrier mobility and effective conduction pathways relative to an ideal crystal.

Existing analytical approaches typically assume perfect, defect-free crystals and therefore fail to capture experimentally relevant defect-induced scattering and electronic-state changes in high-entropy alloys.
The claimed improvement is limited to the stated temperature ranges and to samples having a defect landscape and oxygen level close to the modeled specimen.
Significantly different impurity levels or temperatures outside the stated ranges may require additional calibration.
Single-site CPA can average out complex defect interactions and local relaxations.
Electrical conductivity will be measured on approximately 1 wt.% oxygen specimens at multiple temperatures using a four-point probe or a similar method.
A room-temperature prediction error greater than 10%, or errors consistently exceeding ±5% across the temperature ranges, will falsify the hypothesis.
